method.timing: 31 sorted batch means, adaptive >=5ms calibration capped at 2^20 iterations; nearest-rank p95 (index 29); allocations and output destruction included; fresh process per run/mode; warm calibration; no CPU pinning
method.smoke: 3 samples with one iteration; only 32/128 scalar editing; no memory/profiler; no timing gates

units.allocations: calls to allocation functions per complete profiled process

workloads.typing: insert each scalar then commit; actions = scalars + 1; core constructs a composition per iteration
workloads.editing: insert i/backspace pair at a prefilled active buffer end; setup untimed; divide by 2
workloads.conversion: whole raw string conversion and output destruction; one action
workloads.context_lifecycle: create/focus context, type 13 scalars, Ctrl+Backspace, type again, destroy pending; one cycle
workloads.memory: fresh paired baseline/Jong processes; idle, short pending/cleared, 8192 pending/cleared, 1000/2000 reused+fresh context sessions, context destroyed; see measure-adapter.py
workloads.core_allocations: 1000 convert + new composition/type 13 scalars/backspace/insert i/commit/destroy cycles
workloads.adapter_allocations: 1000 context_lifecycle cycles; paired baseline/Jong; event vector setup once

limits: Batch means are not individual key or key-to-screen tail latency.
No frontend, event loop, retained application document, or desktop acceptance.
RSS/PSS and heap snapshots include framework and allocator caching; paired differences estimate incremental cost.
Retained capacity and heaptrack exit-retention labels do not prove leaks or leak freedom.
Allocation profiles include process/framework startup and teardown; never use profiler timings/RSS as latency or footprint.
Uncontrolled scheduling, thermal state and background activity; no agreed thresholds.
